cards.text: Israel's been on the move a LONG time, and now the book of Numbers stops to look back. Here come the journeys of the Israelites since they came out of the land of Egypt, by their divisions. Every. Single. Stop. Friend, I spent years in one spot in a junk drawer, so a list of places somebody actually WENT gets me excited.

cards.question: The Israelites come out of Egypt by their divisions. Whose leadership are they under?
Moses writes down every stage of Israel's journey. Whose command is he following?

cards.text: Day one is the fifteenth day of the first month, the day after the Passover, and the Israelites set out from Rameses. After everything Egypt put them through, I want to see HOW they walk out that door.

cards.question: How do the Israelites march out of Rameses?

answers.text: Defiantly in full view of the Egyptians
Quietly while nobody was watching them
Slowly behind the chariots of Pharaoh

cards.question: As Israel marches out the day after the Passover, the Egyptians are busy burying all their ___.
True or false: the LORD's judgment in Egypt touched only the people, not Egypt's gods.

cards.text: Then the list REALLY gets going. Set out, camped. Set out, camped. Through the sea into the wilderness, to Elim with its twelve springs and seventy palm trees, to Rephidim where there was no water for the people to drink, to the Wilderness of Sinai, and on and on to Kadesh and Mount Hor at the edge of Edom. Friend, I moved ONE time in my life, from the counter to a drawer, and I'm still not over it.

At the LORD's command, Aaron the priest climbs Mount Hor and dies there at 123 years old, in the fortieth year after Israel came out of Egypt. And the Canaanite king of Arad, down in the Negev, hears that the Israelites are coming.

From Mount Hor it's set out, camped all over again, past the border of Moab to the mountains of Abarim facing Nebo. And the last stop on the list? The plains of Moab, by the Jordan, across from Jericho. That's the longest "are we there yet" I have EVER heard, and every step of it got written down.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "are we there yet", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card runs past 3 sentences: two full sentences, the three one-word fragments "Every. Single. Stop.", and then a fourth sentence with the junk-drawer joke. Cut it down to 3 sentences, for example by folding the joke into one of the others or dropping the fragments.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Slowly behind the chariots of Pharaoh" doesn't make sense for a people leaving Egypt. No baker would take it as a real option, so it reads as filler. Replace it with a believable way of leaving that is false in the passage, like "In a hurry before the sun came up".

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he moved only one time in his life, from the counter to a drawer. His backstory has him start in a bin at a closing bakery, go home with Mother Miller, later go into the drawer, and then be called up to the Dorinverse. The joke changes his established story. Rework it so it stays true to the backstory, for example by joking about the years he spent sitting in one drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The camping list in Numbers 33:5-49 is one long stretch, but it is summed up across three story cards (8, 9 and 10). Aaron's death and the king of Arad (33:38-40) are a short story inside that list, so they belong to the stretch and should not be split off. Merge cards 8 to 10 into one summary card for 33:5-49. Aaron's death on Mount Hor at 123 can be the standout detail on that card.

rule.text: The rule: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A short story inside the stretch, like Nimrod in the list of nations (Genesis 10:8–12), is part of the stretch: it can be the standout detail on that card, but it gets no choice cards.
